paper_verdict.estimator_family: system GMM (two-step, Blundell-Bond type; internal instruments)
paper_verdict.pooling_concerns: Outcome is annual % growth of GDP per capita (not productivity or output level). Exposure enters in levels (per 100 people) with current and one-year lag having opposite signs, so single coefficients do not give net effects. Many rows are interaction main effects or interaction terms (conditional effects). Same 41-country sample reused across columns. Sargan p-values of about 0.99-1.00 suggest instrument proliferation. Working paper (MSE WP 165/2017); mixed-income 41-country sample, years 2004-2015. Fixed telephony and ICT goods imports are not mobile/internet adoption measures.

paper_verdict.estimator_family: OLS in first (and three-year) differences with year dummies and cluster-robust SE (fixed-effects-equivalent); rreg robust regression in appendix Tables A3/A4
paper_verdict.pooling_concerns: Authors acknowledge possible endogeneity but find no instrument and cannot use GMM, so no identification strategy. Exposure is log change in cellular licensed IoT connections per inhabitant (a proxy, not IoT capital); coefficient is a TFP-growth spillover elasticity in log differences, and rounding to 2 decimals in appendix tables. Outcome is TFP growth (productivity). Rows are overlapping specifications on the same 82-country, 2010-2017 sample (with/without MBB, first vs three-year differences, labor definitions, rreg with different outlier-inclusive samples); not independent. Three-year differences are overlapping windows. The paper also contains a separate growth-accounting simulation (Section 6) which is not among these estimates.
